input.task: What does the first 'Add to cart' link on the case-twins page say?

provenance: PR #60 R1, the HIGH finding: T-M42-20 widened both name tiers to case-insensitive, and `_resolve_in`'s `index` branch selects from the match SET before the `n == 1` uniqueness check or any ambiguity bookkeeping runs — so widening the matcher silently moved which element `index` indexes. `case-twins.html` puts `ADD TO CART` (literally uppercase in the MARKUP, which is what makes it a different string to the locator engine) in document order before `Add to cart`. The fix is ordering, not a new guard: each name tier is now two passes, case-exact first and case-folded only if that finds nothing, and — since ADR-032, which PR #60 R10 forced — those two passes are ONE match set chosen once, not two sets selected from in turn. That is what makes the byte-for-byte claim true: a page carrying an exact-case match never consults the fold, for `index` as well as for uniqueness. While it was two sets, `index: 1` on this very fixture returned the same element as `index: 0`; `resolver-index-selects-from-one-match-set` is that case.

triage.red_first: on `fbe304b` the run succeeds and answers `Promo banner offer` — the promo banner, whose accessible name is `ADD TO CART`. Base `6b016b5` answers `Catalogue row CTA`. As a case: `answer 'Promo banner offer' != expected 'Catalogue row CTA'`. At the resolver: `resolve({'role':'link','name':'Add to cart','index':0})` returned `['promo']` on fbe304b and `['rowcta']` on base and after the fix.
triage.note: Each twin is named by `aria-label` and READS something else, so the two answers differ by more than case — `verifier.normalize` folds case, so a fixture whose twins were named by their own text would pass on the wrong element and grade nothing (found while writing this case). `extract_all` grew the same way and is covered by the same ordering fix rather than by a third case; the before/after measurement is in tasks/reviews/pr60-r1-resolution.json.
